summary: Social coverage carried the week's heaviest negative weight: 32% of the 106 social-tagged articles landed negative, well above political (22%) and far above economic (6%). That gap traces to a run of hard-safety stories rather than diffuse gloom: the Sorange coalfield explosion near Quetta that killed all 34 trapped miners, the suicide bombing at Kabal police station in Swat that killed at least 14 (later revised to 17) and drew a UN Security Council condemnation, and a Lahore case in which a police officer was accused of raping a woman inside a station, prompting the suspension of over 70 staff. These are discrete, verifiable incidents, not editorializing, which is why they pulled the social read down sharply.

Political sentiment was the second-most negative category, driven largely by Azad Jammu and Kashmir's second-phase elections, which recurred as a story almost daily this week. PPP repeatedly alleged rigging, ballot stuffing, and coercion, including a disputed party worker's death that PML-N attributed to natural causes; PML-N ultimately took a commanding lead in the results. A separate thread of intra-government friction ran alongside it, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi's call for a governance "reset" and new provinces drew public pushback from Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and PPP's Raza Rabbani, while a stalled presidential sign-off on judicial appointments kept surfacing as a constitutional friction point through the week.

Economic sentiment stayed comparatively mild, only 6% negative across the week, and the one clearly market-relevant flagged story sat outside Pakistan entirely: President Trump's warning that Iran must reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face being "hit very hard," flagged for high market relevance given the route's importance to global oil flows and, by extension, import-dependent economies like Pakistan's. Domestically, the coal mine explosion was the week's clearest economic-and-social overlap, a fatal loss of workforce and disrupted output at a local level, but it didn't push the broader economic tally into negative territory the way the AJK disputes and security incidents did for political and social readings.

Despite how politically charged the week was, coverage stayed largely balanced: of the flagged stories reviewed, all but one carried a "balanced" lean, reporting rigging allegations, ministerial disputes, and protest claims alongside on-record rebuttals from the other side. The one exception, a piece on PTI's call for a fresh vote of confidence, leaned pro-opposition, and the AI's own confidence note flagged why: it was working from a one-sided RSS excerpt rather than the full article. Confidence readings dipped lowest on the AJK election-violence claims themselves, gunfire and ballot-stuffing allegations that the Election Commission and PML-N both disputed as unverified, which is the kind of contested claim worth reading with real caution rather than as settled fact.

notableStories.headline: Quetta coal mine explosion: Search and rescue operation concludes as last two bodies recovered
notableStories.context: A methane explosion and mine collapse at the Sorange coalfield killed all 34 trapped miners, most of them teenagers and young men from Shangla district, marking one of the week's deadliest single incidents and a stark example of recurring mine-safety failures.

notableStories.headline: Suicide bombing at Swat police station kills 14, injures over 25
notableStories.context: A suicide bomber detonated explosives at Kabal police station's gate during a nearby anti-terrorism protest; the attack, later condemned by the UN Security Council, was the week's most significant security incident and a driver of the sharply negative social and political readings.

notableStories.headline: Trump warns Iran to open Strait of Hormuz or get 'hit very hard'
notableStories.context: Trump threatened Iran over continued shipping attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, a key global oil corridor; flagged for high market relevance since disruption there would raise oil prices for import-dependent economies including Pakistan's.

notableStories.headline: Second phase of AJK polls concludes amid renewed rigging allegations by PPP
notableStories.context: PPP accused PML-N of stealing votes "through bullets, batons and coercion" and cited a disputed party worker's death, while PML-N attributed the death to natural causes; this dispute recurred across multiple days and was the week's dominant political storyline.

notableStories.headline: Cop allegedly rapes woman inside Lahore police station; entire staff suspended
notableStories.context: An assistant sub-inspector allegedly raped a mentally impaired woman inside a Lahore police station, prompting the suspension of the entire station staff of over 70 personnel, a case that speaks directly to the week's weak spot in institutional trust and public safety.
